messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up on hetero-pinning policy + tenant fairness. TL;DR: Add a per-tenant "soft-pin" budget that lets hot shards keep VRAM for a few seconds without hard eviction, but still allows global defrag under emergency. Looking for tradeoffs and API shape.

aj: Main concern: how do we enforce global fairness? soft-pins sound good but noisy tenant could hog budgets. maybe a token bucket per-tenant + global reclaim priority.

sachin: agree with token-bucket. also need a fast path for small allocs: if alloc < 128KB, bypass soft-pin and treat as ephemeral. prevents tiny requests from eating budget.

maria: good point. thinking: two buckets: long_soft_pin (secs) and micro_pin (ms). long consumes credits. micro is free but only for small pages.

lia: how do we surface this in the allocator API? two flags? e.g. alloc( size, pin_hint=SOFT_LONG | SOFT_MICRO ) or an enum.
aj: enum + struct makes sense so future fields (priority, ttl) can be added. e.g.:
```c
struct PinHint {
  enum type { NONE, MICRO, SOFT_LONG } t;
  uint32_t ttl_ms; // 0 -> default
  uint8_t priority; // 0..255, higher = less likely to be reclaimed
};
```

sachin: reclaim logic: soft-pins should be evicted under two conditions: 1) global OOM/compaction trigger; 2) tenant exhausted credits. Need graceful demotion (reduce priority) not instant evict.

maria: demotion sounds right. maybe an eviction waterfall: SOFT_LONG -> SOFT_MICRO -> NONE, with a cooldown to avoid oscillation.

lia: telemetry: we should emit per-tenant pin-credit usage + demote/evict events. Will need a tag on pages: tenant_id + pin_type + expiry_ts.

aj: tags add overhead; use a sidecar slab table mapping page_id -> metadata. hashed, lock-free lookup. cheaper than per-page header.

sachin: can we leverage existing kv-cache stripe? reuse stripe index so we don't add more structures. also simplifies compaction scans.

maria: nice idea. reuse stripe index + add compacted bitset for soft-pins. We'll need to update compactor to treat soft-pinned pages as scavengable only when credits exhausted.

lia: operator UX: config knobs per-tenant: credits/sec, burst_credits, micro_window_ms. Default sensible values for single-tenant vs multi-tenant.

aj: backward compatibility: if not specified, default to 0 (no soft pins) so behavior unchanged. opt-in per-tenant.

maria: rollout plan: 1) implement allocator API + sidecar metadata; 2) dry-run telemetry mode (do not actually demote/evict, just log what would happen); 3) enable soft-pin for internal perf tests; 4) gradual enable for customers behind feature flag.

offload-bot: deploy-check: canary-group=redwood-runtime-candidates, rollout=10%, monitor=pin_credit_exhaustion, evict_rate, p99_lat.

lia: outstanding questions: a) how to compute credit cost per page (weight by size/seq_len?) b) can we prioritize by model type (embedding vs generative) c) interaction with spill-to-disk policies.

sachin: propose credit cost = size_kb * (1 + 0.5 * seq_factor) where seq_factor in [0,1] derived from recent usage. model-type priority is orthogonal — assign tenant profile boosting score.

aj: interaction with spill: soft-pins should prevent async spill for their TTL, but on global pressure we still allow spill. we must avoid double-accounting costs in billing.

maria: OK next actions: aj + sachin draft allocator API PR + pseudo-code for reclaim waterfall. lia drafts telemetry events and config schema. I'll write the rollout checklist and canary metrics.

lia: ping me when PRs are ready, I'll append monitoring dashboards.

aj: starting PR now, will include unit tests for token-bucket leak and demotion edgecases.

sachin: I'll prototype sidecar table in a branch and run local compactor sim to measure overhead.

maria: thanks all. tagging for follow-up: @lia @aj @sachin — please drop updates here. :sparkles:
